paper_summary: An engineering development paper on a 'C'-sandwich radome (three E-glass/epoxy skins with two low-dielectric cores) for underwater antenna systems. Flat and semi-cylindrical configurations were compared by ANSYS finite element analysis under external hydrostatic pressure (flat: 0.83 mm deflection, Tsai-Wu index 1.73, factor of safety 0.57; hemispherical/semi-cylindrical: 0.161 mm deflection, Tsai-Wu index 0.7605, factor of safety 1.4), and the selected semi-cylindrical radome, fabricated by matched-die moulding with hand-laid machined cores and a bolted titanium flange with O-ring and rubber sealant, passed the external pressure test. Syntactic foam is named only as the core material; no properties, composition or test data for the foam itself are reported.
extraction_notes: Off-topic for this dataset. The paper is a structural/manufacturing development study of an underwater C-sandwich radome, not a study of hollow-particle composites. 'Syntactic foam' appears only as a generic label for the sandwich core material ('the core material is syntactic foam / epoxy'); the paper reports NO matrix or particle identity, no microballoon type/grade/size/wall thickness, no volume or weight fraction, no density, no porosity, and no measured mechanical, thermal or hydrostatic property of the foam. The only quantitative results are structure-level FEA outputs for the whole radome (maximum deflection 0.83 mm flat vs 0.161 mm hemispherical D-type; Tsai-Wu strength index 1.73 vs 0.7605; inferred factors of safety 0.57 vs 1.4, with a 0.5 mm allowable deflection) plus the pressure-test ramp procedure (4 bar/min in four equal stages, 3 min hold per stage, 1 h hold at test pressure, destructive test to 1.5x test pressure held 1 min). The actual test pressure value is not stated (likely withheld for defence reasons). None of these map onto composition x test-condition records for a hollow-particle composite, and the text explicitly says the constituent properties used in the FEA came from tests on standard specimens that are not reported here. Records is therefore empty per rule 6/10.
